- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile.  
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days.  
- Adjust forecasts downward if recent 18-day history shows mean reversion toward lower levels.  
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; lagged sentiment (e.g., 3–5 day average) better predicts direction.  
- Reduce forecast magnitude if true outcome deviates >10% from 30-day moving average of history.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes, reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, allow slight upward bias but cap at 1.5x recent high.  
- Correct for “sentiment lag” — if sentiment turns negative after forecast peak, reduce forecast by 3–5% per day.
